subject: microbiology
title: Staphylococcal Toxins: Protein A, Panton-Valentine Leukocidin and Toxic Shock Toxin

steps.tx: **Protein A** coats S aureus and binds IgG by its Fc stem, presenting antibody backwards so phagocyte Fc receptors find nothing useful, while also engaging Fab VH3 families as a B cell superantigen. Coagglutination tests exploit it (antibody coated staphylococci as reagent carriers), turning a virulence factor into bench equipment.
steps.say: Antibody grabbed by the stem cannot call phagocytes; protein A reverses the uniform.

left.title: Protein A actions
points: B cell superantigen via VH3 Fab
Von Willebrand factor binding in endocarditis

right.title: Protein A uses
points: Latex kit component for aureus identification

steps.tx: **Panton Valentine leukocidin** (PVL) is a two component pore toxin (LukS and LukF) lysing neutrophils and macrophages, genetically mobile (prophage), marking community MRSA and MSSA strains that cause recurrent boils and necrotising pneumonia after influenza, especially in the young. Its presence changes severity expectations, not first antibiotic choice.
steps.say: PVL kills the very cells sent to kill it; necrotising pneumonia in a young adult asks its name.

right.title: PVL practice
points: Notification and typing in outbreaks by jurisdiction

steps.tx: **Toxic shock syndrome toxin 1** (TSST 1) is a superantigen (antigens lesson) flooding T cells into cytokine storm: menstrual cases with vaginal colonisation and tampon traditions, non menstrual from wound and post surgical colonisation, presenting fever, rash, desquamation later, hypotension and multi organ failure, diagnosed clinically with cultures usually sterile at the toxin's distant stage.
steps.say: Toxin made elsewhere shocks everywhere; blood cultures are usually innocent in toxic shock.

left.title: TSS portrait
points: Fever, diffuse rash, then desquamation 1 to 2 weeks
Hypotension and three organ systems minimum

right.title: TSS answers
points: Remove tampon or drain focus, wash out
Anti staphylococcal therapy plus clindamycin toxin suppression
IVIG considered in streptococcal toxic shock

steps.tx: **Superantigen family** extends enterotoxins and exfoliatins: TSST and enterotoxin B and C crosslink MHC II to TCR V beta subsets, each toxin a V beta signature, explaining cytokine patterns and why toxoid protection is hard. Staphylococcal superantigen like proteins additionally block complement and neutrophil recruitment, layered immune evasion.
steps.say: Each superantigen shakes hands with a different V beta family and storms accordingly.

left.title: Superantigen roster
points: TSST 1: menstrual and non menstrual TSS
Enterotoxins B, C: non menstrual and food roles
Exfoliative toxins: serine proteases more than classic superantigens

right.title: Evasion partners
points: SSL proteins block complement and IgA

steps.tx: **Alpha toxin** (haemolysin alpha) forms beta barrel pores in membranes including red cells (the beta haemolysis partly), platelets, endothelium, driving dermonecrosis and pneumonia injury, while beta toxin (sphingomyelinase, hot cold phenomenon), gamma toxin and delta toxin complete the haemolysin alphabet students inherit.
steps.say: Alpha pores perforate the neighbourhood; beta needs cold to finish its haemolysis trick.

left.title: Alpha toxin
points: Pore forming cytolysin broad cell range

steps.tx: **Agr quorum sensing** conducts the toxin orchestra: at high cell density the agr system upregulates secreted toxins and downregulates surface adhesins, switching aureus from colonising to attacking programme, a regulatory biography explaining abscess timing and why stationary phase culture supernatants are toxic.
steps.say: Crowded aureus turns toxin loud and adhesive quiet; density conducts the programme.

nodes.label: Low density: adhesins on, toxins quiet (colonise)

steps.tx: **Toxin suppressing antibiotics** (clindamycin and linezolid protein synthesis inhibitors from the pharmacology lessons) join cell wall agents in severe toxin mediated disease (toxic shock, necrotising fasciitis and pneumonia) to stop new toxin production while bactericidal partners clear organisms, an adjunct logic the bench toxins justify.
steps.say: Kill the factory and silence it: clindamycin joins beta lactams where toxins drive disease.

left.title: Adjunct logic
points: Protein synthesis stop halts toxin production
Eagle effect: stationary cells evade penicillin killing
IVIG neutralisation debated, streptococcal TSS stronger case

right.title: Syndromes applying it
points: Toxin mediated disease after source control

steps.tx: **Laboratory toxin detection** is mostly research and reference work (PVL gene PCR in defined syndromes, toxin typing in outbreaks, enterotoxin immunoassays in food), while routine laboratories report species and susceptibility and clinicians diagnose toxin disease clinically. Knowing which requests reference laboratories actually answer prevents specimen theatre.
steps.say: Toxin genes belong to defined syndromes and outbreaks, not routine wound reports.

left.title: Reference testing
points: lukS F PCR for PVL in severe presentations
Exfoliative toxin genes in scalded skin investigations
Whole genome virulence profiling in outbreaks

right.title: Routine reporting
points: Food poisoning diagnosis clinical and epidemiological
